result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A keeps the payload tighter (one subset variable file or at most two weights), and A asks outright about language and script coverage instead of assuming Latin. A also gets the 'friendly' feel from sizes, weights, spacing and a zero-byte Roboto option. B is solid and covers tabular figures well, but it allows 3–4 static files, starts by assuming Latin script, and wrongly claims Roboto has the same x-height as Nunito Sans. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B is the better answer. It asks up front which languages and scripts the vendors read, includes a zero-byte system-font option that gets the friendly feel from spacing, color and rounded corners, and keeps the bundle to one variable file or two weights. A has sound bundling and tabular-figure advice, but it assumes Latin script from the start and makes questionable claims: that Nunito Sans and Roboto share x-height behavior and that the system font covers every language. Neither stack is fully free of assumptions about which font a given Android phone has, and B's mention of Swahili diacritics is slightly off.
